_comment: THE bc24 ACCEPTED-DIVERGENCE LEDGER. `parity-oracle-bc24`'s Tier C is
BLOCKING AGAINST THIS FILE: the job computes the first divergent round of
every whole 2000-round game, for every (bot, map) pair, and FAILS if
(a) a pair diverges and has no entry here, (b) a pair diverges EARLIER
than its entry, (c) an entry no longer reproduces -- a stale excuse is as
bad as a missing one -- or (d) any divergence occurs while the traced
bytecode peak is still inside the tier's ceiling, which on this year's
evidence means always, and therefore means a real rules bug rather than
an instrumentation artefact.
IT IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE PHASE-30 EXIT CONDITION THE DESIGN NOTE
COMMITTED TO. All fifteen pairs -- three bots (`examplefuncsplayer`, the
scenario bot and its teleport variant) across five `small` maps -- are
bit-exact against the published battlecode24-3.0.5 jar for all 2000
rounds, on every field of every record: crumbs, captures, pickups, level
sums, upgrade masks and points, and per duck the position, health, both
cooldowns, all three experiences, the carried flag and roundsAlive, IN
EXEC ORDER, plus every flag's location, its object-identity start-location
flag, its carrier and its dropped-round counter.
The measured bytecode headroom is what makes a whole-game window
defensible: the example bot peaked at 297..783 of the 25 000 limit
(1.2..3.2 %) with ZERO mid-turn cut-offs, and the scenario bot at
796..940 (3.2..3.8 %). Both are recorded in docs/PARITY.md section bc24.
An entry, if one is ever needed, looks like:
{"bot": "...", "map": "...", "first_divergent_round": N,
"cause": "<one sentence naming a ROOT CAUSE>",
"docs": "PARITY.md#bc24"}
and 'unknown' is not a cause -- that is precisely the close state the
operator ruled unacceptable on 2026-09-03.
